text:
alex: FYI customer reported deploys failing intermittently since 03:00 UTC — job logs show 403 on artifact upload to gs://redwood-builds.
olivia: hitting them now, they say it started after we rolled out the runner-proxy change yesterday.
tara: can you paste the exact error from the CI logs?
olivia: here: 
```
Uploading artifact to gs://redwood-builds/prod/237.tar.gz
ERROR: Upload failed: 403 Forbidden: The caller does not have permission to access the object.
at upload.go:142
```
alex: job uses ci-deploy-bot SA via runner proxy (OIDC -> impersonation). Token looks valid but upload denied.
ci-runner-bot: deploy job id=237, runner=runner-us-west-2-7, duration=10m 12s, upload step failed at 9m45s.
kevin: suspect impersonation token TTL / caching. We shortened the proxy cache to 60s to reduce long-lived creds. If the upload stream is long it might refresh mid-upload and cause ephemeral credential mismatch.
tara: that's different from previous rotation issues — almost like a mid-stream credential swap causes the storage backend to reject with 403.
alex: can we reproduce locally? steps from customer: 
1) start upload large file (~200MB) using gsutil with service token from proxy
2) trigger proxy to refresh token during upload (curl refresh endpoint)
3) observe 403
kevin: repro attempt: 
```bash
# get token from runner-proxy
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $JOB_TOKEN" https://proxy.internal/sa-token > token.b64
cat token.b64 | base64 -d > sa.json
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=sa.json
dd if=/dev/zero of=bigfile bs=1M count=200
gsutil cp bigfile gs://redwood-builds/test-large.bin
# in parallel trigger proxy refresh
curl -X POST https://proxy.internal/admin/refresh?job=237
```
kevin: when I force a refresh mid-upload I reproduces a 403 on gsutil for large transfers.
olivia: customer confirmed they do large docker pushes (~300MB layers) and the failures align with long uploads.
tara: OK root cause hypothesis: runner-proxy rotates/refreshes impersonation token out from under an in-flight upload. Storage validates the signed token used at start vs the one presented mid-stream and rejects.
alex: why would storage reject a refreshed token? Shouldn't uploads use a single bearer for the connection? Maybe chunked uploads re-open connections and pick up new headers.
kevin: uploads use resumable sessions: the resumable upload session ID is bound to the credentials used to start the session. If the token is swapped, subsequent PUTs for the session present different auth and GCS rejects with 403.
tara: interesting — means short-lived token window has to span the full expected upload time plus jitter. Our previous change decreased the impersonation window to 60s; long uploads exceed that.
olivia: customer workaround: retry job when failure happens, usually succeeds on retry because new session starts with fresh token.
alex: action items? short-term: increase proxy impersonation TTL for upload-heavy jobs. Long-term: make the proxy pin credentials for the life of a resumable upload session or implement session-affinity for tokens.
kevin: immediate fix: bump proxy token lease to 20m for "ci-deploy" role. Also add check in runner to detect resumable upload and pin token until session finalizes.
tara: also update RBAC — instead of broad storage.admin we should give ci-deploy-bot storage.objectCreator + storage.objects.get for least privilege.
devops-bot: created internal ticket INF-4921 to track: "ci-runner: resumable upload token pinning + increase impersonation window" and assigned to kevin/tara; link https://console.redwood.ai/infra/INF-4921
alex: I've informed customer and suggested retry loop for now, and that we're rolling a config patch.
olivia: customer replied :thumbsup: appreciates temporary workaround.
kevin: rolling proxy config change to staging now (increase lease to 20m for ci-deploy). Will monitor.
tara: I'll add a unit/integration test to simulate mid-upload refreshes and fail the build if we regress.
alex: thanks team. please post follow-up in thread when staging patch is green and when prod rollout is scheduled.
kevin: staging patch succeeded, no 403s in simulated runs. Scheduling prod rollover in 30m and will watch logs.
alex: noted. marking resolved for now until prod rollout completes.
